gaps.title: The darkness class is a stated rule, not validated against measured on-water light
gaps.whyItMatters: DARKNESS_RULE_V1 reuses the Engine's DarknessFactor constants (cloud knee 50 %, span 50 %, city glow 0.3) and its label thresholds. Nobody has measured whether the moonlight index orders real nights by on-water illuminance.
gaps.bowfisherDecision: Which nights are darkest on the water.
gaps.stopCondition: Stop when a preregistered comparison against an independent illuminance dataset (public sky-quality or lux records near fleet lakes) is scored, or the owner rejects the need.
gaps.expectedOutput: A scored comparison and a keep/adjust recommendation for DARKNESS_RULE_V1.

humanOrFieldValidationRequired.what: OPTIONAL: sky-quality-meter readings from a boat may be added as evidence; they are never required.

gaps.title: Cloud cover from the Weather Brain is mapped, declared and tested on Weather-built states, but not read live
gaps.whyItMatters: Without a Weather state every night is answered MOON_ONLY (the clear-sky upper bound). The input reads the Weather state (sector-brain-weather-state-v1) and is declared in brain.json consumes. Tests use schema-valid states built by the Weather Brain from its recorded NWS fixtures (2 lakes, 2 run times each) plus schema-valid variants. A state holds 12 forecast hours, so cloud covers only the part of the window still ahead at the Weather run, and only runs from about 3 h before astronomical dusk cover a whole night. Nothing reads /lakes/{k}/states/weather live while both Brains are disabled, and no live Weather state has been checked.
gaps.bowfisherDecision: Whether an overcast night with a bright moon is still dark on the water.
gaps.stopCondition: Stop when, at enablement, the Moon run reads each lake's Weather state from RTDB (with the dependency's freshness rule) instead of a --weather file, and the MOON_AND_CLOUD share over a week of live runs is recorded.
gaps.expectedOutput: A consumes entry for the Weather Brain and a mapping test.

gaps.title: No per-lake skyglow input
gaps.whyItMatters: Cloud reflects city glow near towns instead of blocking moonlight. The rule uses the Engine's fixed default (0.3) for every lake.
gaps.bowfisherDecision: Whether a lake near a city is darker under cloud.
gaps.stopCondition: Stop when a public artificial-sky-brightness dataset is bound per lake, or the owner decides the default is enough.
gaps.expectedOutput: A per-lake skyglow factor in the knowledge release, or a recorded decision to keep the default.
